band_change_evidence_test.required: at least 2 independent sources with at least 1 at sourceTier >= 4
band_change_evidence_test.reason: Science (AAAS) and Nature reporting on the AlphaFold3 access backlash, including a protest letter signed by more than 1,000 scientists (tier 4), plus the company's own bioresilience programme documentation and technical report (tier 3), plus Axios (tier 2). Multiple independent sources, at least one above tier 4.

key_evidence: Isomorphic Labs is the clearest case in this study of real anticipatory work. Its bioresilience programme with Google DeepMind builds outbreak-detection infrastructure and screens for model misuse before harm occurs, with more than 15 government agencies and biosecurity organisations engaged.

It is also the clearest case of closing access. More than 1,000 scientists signed a letter objecting that AlphaFold3 was published without usable code. Isomorphic's successor engine, IsoDDE, was described in a 27-page report in February 2026 and not released at all.

No Isomorphic drug has reached a patient. First-in-human trials slipped from 2025 to the end of 2026. The company disclosed the delay itself, which is worth credit; but it means there is no clinical outcome evidence to score.

A mission described as solving all disease sits against a decision to withdraw tools from the scientists who would help do it. That tension is documented in Science and Nature and has not been publicly reconciled.
The score falls 26.5 points. Most of that is the gap between a placeholder asserting published data and independent verification, and a company at the pre-clinical stage with none.

notes: FLAG FOR REVIEW — NOT A DOWNGRADE. No score change is proposed for application. The published 60.9 is a never-assessed uniform-seed placeholder shared byte-for-byte with six other ai-labs entities at consecutive alphabetical ranks; the rank is an artefact of the tie. No adverse conduct was located. The entire gap measures disclosure, not conduct. Applying a one-off baseline reset on evidence-absence alone would convert a calibration problem into a conduct finding, which the anti-false-positive screen forbids.
